about.repoDescription: The app's open-source code on GitHub.

recovery.label: Reopen windows on launch
recovery.description: Which of the windows open when you last quit Vertex (or when it crashed) are reopened when it starts. Each comes back at its size and place, with its tabs.

language.title: Language
language.label: App language
language.description: The language of menus and the interface.

channel.label: Update channel
channel.description: The release channel Vertex updates from.
channel.loadFailed: Couldn't load channels from the update server: {error}

token.label: Channel token
token.description: Optional token for restricted channels. Stored in your system keychain.
token.saved: A token is saved in your system keychain.

theme.title: Theme
theme.previewText: Markdown, links and code use the editor fonts below.
theme.primaryDescription: Buttons, links, selection and focus rings.
theme.colorModeDescription: Light, dark, or follow the system.
theme.radiusDescription: How rounded buttons, inputs and panels are.
theme.editorMonoFontDescription: Code blocks and inline code in notes.
theme.customCssDescription: Added after Vertex's own styles. Saved when you leave the editor.
theme.customCssUntrusted: This workspace's CSS is off until you trust the workspace: it could restyle or hide anything, the trust prompt included.

view.title: View
view.statusBarDescription: Display mode of the status bar.
view.selectionToolbarDescription: Show a formatting toolbar above selected text.
view.slashMenuDescription: Type / to open a menu of blocks to insert.
view.blockHandleDescription: Show a handle beside blocks to drag or move them.
view.headerHistoryDescription: Where the header shows undo and redo.
view.headerFormattingDescription: Where the header shows bold, italic, strikethrough and highlight.
view.panelsDescription: Which views each side panel has, in what order, and how you switch between them. Rearrange them here, or by dragging or right-clicking their buttons in a window.
view.panelStyleDescription: Buttons inside the panels, or icon strips at the window’s edges (click the shown view’s icon to collapse its panel).
view.panelLayoutDescription: Drag views between the sides and Hidden; right-click one to move it, hide it or add a separator.
view.updateLinks: Update links after a move or rename
view.updateLinksDescription: When a note or folder is moved or renamed, what happens to the links that pointed to it. Ask is the default; the dialog's Remember choice sets it for a workspace.
view.deletedFilesDescription: Where Delete in Files sends items. The Trash and the workspace’s .trash folder (hidden from Files) can be undone; deleting permanently asks first and cannot be undone.
view.attachmentsFolderDescription: Where files from outside the workspace go when chat or a note takes them, and pasted screenshots. Created when first needed.

trust.title: Trust
trust.trustedDescription: Programs here (workflows) run without asking, and a trusted workspace's own settings apply: its custom CSS, the plugins it turns on, its AI and git settings. Everything else asks first.
trust.noTrusted: Nothing yet. A workflow’s first run or a workspace’s settings ask you, or add a folder or file here.
trust.unreadable: “{name}” can’t be read as a program
trust.fileTrustDescription: Paths and content: a trusted file, or a trusted folder's programs as they were when you trusted it, run only while unchanged outside Vertex; edits in Vertex keep them trusted, and a program added or changed elsewhere (sync, git, another app, a workflow) asks first. Paths: anything at a trusted path runs.

plugins.title: Plugins
plugins.coreDescription: Built into Vertex. Turning one off removes what it adds once Vertex restarts.

reason.missing: Off: it needs {name}, which isn't installed
reason.requirementOff: Off: it needs {name}, which is off

plugins.untrusted: This workspace turns on plugins that are off in your settings. They run once you trust it.

restart.title: Restart Vertex to turn off {name}?
restart.description: It keeps running until Vertex restarts. Your workspace windows open again after the restart.

plugins.settingsWaitForTrust: Some of this workspace's changes here apply only once you trust it.
plugins.communityDescription: Installed by you, for every workspace. A community plugin runs as Vertex does: it can read and change your notes and files.
plugins.upToDate: Every plugin is up to date.
plugins.checkAutomaticallyDescription: At launch and daily, Vertex asks each plugin's repository for its newest version: one request per plugin, carrying nothing about you; the host sees only the address it comes from. Updates install only when you accept them.

origin.unknown: Installed before Vertex kept where plugins come from
origin.copied: Put in the workspace by hand or by sync

plugins.ownCopyHere: This workspace has its own copy
plugins.workspaceDescription: Plugins in this workspace's .vertex/plugins folder, which travel with it, and the ones it turns on that this device doesn't have. They run only in this workspace, once it's trusted and each one is accepted as it is.
plugins.noneInWorkspace: This workspace has no plugins of its own.
plugins.notAccepted: New or changed since it was accepted: it runs once you review it
plugins.missing: This workspace turns it on, but this device doesn't have it
plugins.missingFrom: The workspace says it comes from {source}
plugins.missingNoSource: The workspace doesn't say where it comes from

trustModal.trustDescription: Its workspace has plugins. Trusting it runs them, as they are now.
trustModal.acceptDescription: These are new, or changed since they were accepted (by sync, Git or another app). They run as they are now.

installModal.title: Install {name}?
installModal.claims: It says it's from {origin}, but it wasn't fetched from there.
installModal.otherOrigin: An installed plugin already has the id "{id}" ({installed}). This one comes from elsewhere: it would replace that plugin and get its settings, data and secrets.
installModal.noPermissions: Nothing beyond what every plugin gets.
installModal.warning: A plugin runs as Vertex does: it can read, change and delete your notes and files. Install it only if you trust where it came from.

urlModal.title: Install from a URL
urlModal.description: A link to a .zip of the plugin's folder.

gitModal.title: Install from a Git repository
gitModal.description: GitHub, GitLab, Gitea or Forgejo, public: a link to the repository, a branch or a release.
gitModal.noRelease: Its latest release (none has a plugin.zip)
gitModal.branchHint: Follows the branch: each new commit is an update.

removeModal.title: Remove {name}?
removeModal.description: Its files are deleted. Its settings and data stay, for if you install it again.

scope.label: Editing
scope.help: A workspace's own settings live in its .vertex/settings.json and override yours there.
scope.globalOnlyPage: A workspace can't change these settings; they apply everywhere.

ui.selectFile: Select a file from the left side.

filetree.newFileDescription: Creates a new Markdown file in the workspace root.
filetree.newFolderDescription: Creates a new folder in the workspace root.
filetree.importFailed: Could not add the dropped items.
filetree.copyFailed: Could not copy to the clipboard.
filetree.nothingToPaste: The clipboard has no files to paste.
filetree.trashedWorkspace: Moved {count} item(s) to the workspace’s .trash folder.
filetree.undoSkipped: Some items were left as they are, since they changed or moved after that step: {names}
filetree.redoSkipped: Some items were left as they are, since they changed or moved after the undo: {names}
filetree.undoNotLast: Something changed in Files since. Press Cmd/Ctrl+Z in Files to undo the latest change first.

updateLinks.description: {links} link(s) in {files} note(s) point to the old name or place.
updateLinks.remember: Remember my decision for this workspace

conflict.applyToAll: Do this for the remaining {count} conflict(s)

ui.blockHandle: Drag to move block, click for options

ai.stale: The text changed since this was generated. Retry to use the current text.
ai.staleTool: The text changed since this was suggested.
